name: Button
accessibility: A real button element. Loading keeps the label in the tree and sets aria-busy="true". Disabled uses the disabled attribute, or aria-disabled="true" when the reason must stay announceable. An icon-only button needs aria-label from the translation tables. At the 480 width every button is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard. The telegram label (white on #2AABEE, 2.57) is under the 4.5 text floor by the one brand exception of reference/refusals.md.
purpose: An action the user starts.
usage: One primary per view; accent for a deliberate second action; secondary for the quiet alternative; ghost for the link-style action; danger for irreversible actions, which confirm. telegram is the one brand exception and appears only where the Telegram sign-in or WebApp action is offered. A link that navigates is an anchor, not a button.

name: Text field
accessibility: Every control has a visible label bound by for and id. The hint and the message are linked by aria-describedby; an invalid value sets aria-invalid="true" on the control and shows a message with an icon and text, never colour alone. The reveal button does not carry aria-pressed: its accessible name switches between the show and the hide label (data-label-show and data-label-hide, from the translation tables). Fields are 16 px text at the 480 width so phones do not zoom. Border: --border-input at --border-input-width; --border-input-hover on hover.
purpose: Text entry.
usage: One field per label; format hints in the hint line, not in the placeholder; amounts take --num.

name: Radio
accessibility: A native radio input inside a label, grouped in a fieldset with a legend; the arrow keys move inside the group, Tab leaves it. The ring uses --border-input. The row is at least --touch-min high at the 480 width.
purpose: One choice from a short list.
usage: Two to five options visible together; more than five use a select.

name: Toggle
accessibility: A native checkbox with role="switch". The state is carried by the knob position and the track colour, and announced by the switch role. The knob uses --on-primary on the primary track so it keeps 3:1 at night. The row is at least --touch-min high at the 480 width.
purpose: A setting that takes effect at once.
usage: Statements ("E-mail notifications"); a choice that needs a Save button is a checkbox.

name: Card

variants.brand: ds-card--brand: a summary on the primary colour; text --on-primary, quiet text --on-primary-muted, the sign of a figure written in the text
variants.media: ds-card--media: a cover (.ds-card__media, an img or the fallback with an icon), a chip on the photo (.ds-card__tag) and .ds-card__content

accessibility: An interactive card holds exactly one link in its title; the link stretches over the card and takes the focus outline for the whole card. No click handler on the container. The title is a heading whose level fits the page. The brand card's text is --on-primary (8.48 day, 5.85 night) and its quiet text --on-primary-muted (6.63 day, 4.51 night on --primary); a Button inside takes the --on-primary border. A chip on a photo is --text-on-scrim over --scrim-strong (7.63 on a white photo). A cover that only decorates has alt="".
purpose: A bounded group of related content.
usage: The decorative tick is placed by elements/README.md and is not part of this component; a card keeps --border-subtle. The brand card is for a summary; a figure on it takes --on-primary with its sign written, never --success or --danger. The media card is for a cover and its content.

name: Badge

variants.count: ds-badge--count: the number of unread items on an icon button
variants.dot: ds-dot, ds-dot--danger: an unread dot, 8 px

accessibility: A badge always carries text; meaning is never colour alone. Badges use the status subtle ground and subtle text (7.12 and better). A decorative badge is aria-hidden. The count is aria-hidden and the button's aria-label carries the number; --on-danger on --danger is 7.86 day. A dot is never alone: it has role="img" with a text label and the row says it in words.
purpose: A short status label.
usage: One to two words; the status text, not an action. The app caps the count ("99+").

name: Alert
accessibility: role="status" for info and success, role="alert" for warning and danger. The severity is carried by the icon disc, the start bar and the title text. The dismiss button is a real button whose aria-label comes from the translation tables. The tick is never placed on an alert (refusals.md).
purpose: A message the user must see in context.
usage: Short title plus one sentence; an action is a button inside .ds-alert__actions.

name: Tabs
accessibility: role tablist, tab and tabpanel with aria-selected and aria-controls; one tab is in the tab order, Left and Right, Home and End move between tabs (components.js, direction aware), Tab enters the panel. The selected tab is marked by colour and by the underline. The strip scrolls sideways on a phone and each tab is at least --touch-min high.
purpose: Switch between sibling views of one subject.
usage: Two to six tabs; a tab changes the view in place, not the page. Five shell tabs are navigation, not this component.

name: Filter chip
accessibility: A button with aria-pressed; a selected chip also shows the check icon so colour is not alone. A group is a role="group" with an aria-label. A removable chip has a remove button with its own aria-label. The border is --border-input (3.03 day, 3.01 night).
purpose: Filter a list by one value.
usage: A row of chips above a list; the count is mono figures.

name: Tooltip
states: hover (the trigger's, and the tooltip opens)
disabled (a disabled trigger cannot open it)
accessibility: The trigger is a real button or link with class ds-tooltip-trigger and aria-describedby naming the tooltip; the tooltip is role="tooltip", holds text only (no link, button or field: that is a popover) and stays in the tree while hidden so the description resolves. It opens at once, with no delay, on hover (only a pointer that can hover), on keyboard focus and on a tap (components.js toggles data-open; a tap elsewhere closes it); Escape closes it and it stays closed until the pointer or the focus leaves. A transparent border bridges the gap, so the tooltip stays while it is hovered. An icon-only trigger needs aria-label. Ground: --bg-emphasis with --text-inverse (17 or better in both themes). At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: A short hint on one part: what an icon means, why a value is what it is.
usage: Use for a hint of one sentence that no one needs in order to act; a longer text, a link or an action belongs in the page or a popover. The trigger is a ghost icon button (info icon) or the part itself. On a phone nothing opens by hover: the tap is the only way, so the hint is never the only place a needed fact lives. Put data-align on a tooltip near the edge of a screen so it stays in view.

name: Toast
accessibility: Kit fix: the region is aria-live="polite" and present from the start; a toast is inserted into it. A danger toast has role="alert". A dismiss button is present. The toast ground is opaque (the subtle tint over --bg-surface) so the page behind never shows through.
purpose: A short confirmation that needs no decision.
usage: Never the only place a failure shows; auto-hide is the app's and never shorter than the time to read it.

name: Pager
sizes: one size (md height, touch-min on a phone)
accessibility: A nav landmark with an aria-label; a list of links; the current page has aria-current="page" and is filled (not by colour alone: the fill is the brand colour with --on-primary text); each number carries aria-label "Page n", previous and next carry their own aria-label; a disabled end has aria-disabled="true" and no href; the gap is aria-hidden. At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Moves between pages of a list or a table.
usage: Use when a list has pages; show the first, the last, the current and its neighbours with a gap between. Links, not buttons: a page is an address. Do not use for steps of a flow (a stepper) or for panels (Tabs).
notes: The chevron icons are not mirrored for right-to-left now (nothing is mirrored).

name: Progress
accessibility: Kit fix: the track has role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and an accessible name (aria-labelledby or aria-label); indeterminate omits aria-valuenow. The fill width is the custom property --value. Indeterminate motion stops under reduced motion.
purpose: How far a long operation has come.
usage: Show the figure as text beside it.

name: Skeleton
accessibility: The skeleton parts are aria-hidden; the region that will hold the content carries aria-busy="true" and one .ds-sr-only role="status" text (the page's own word for loading); when the content arrives the skeletons and the status go and aria-busy is removed. The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion. The fill is decorative and carries no text.
purpose: Holds the place of content that is loading, in the shape of what will come.
usage: Use for a list, a card or a table that takes more than a moment to arrive; match the shape and the count of the real content. A short wait or a single action uses the Loader (K20); a button uses its own busy state.

name: Loader
accessibility: Kit fix: the wrapper has role="status" and a text (visible or .ds-sr-only) so the busy state is announced. The ring is aria-hidden. Under reduced motion it turns four times slower.
purpose: A wait of unknown length.
usage: Prefer a skeleton for content (batch 2); a loader for a section or a page.

name: Row list

row: linked (one a.ds-row__link stretched over the row)
variants.tone: data-tone="success|warning|danger|accent|neutral" on .ds-row__lead (and on .ds-lead, the same box outside a row); the primary tint without it

accessibility: A ul of li. A linked row holds one anchor on its title; its ::after stretches the hit area over the whole row (the row, not the 26 px anchor, is the touch target); the focus outline is drawn around the row at --focus-offset. Title text-primary, meta text-tertiary on the white --bg-surface of the row only (decided by the owner, 2026-10-17; a row never takes a fill); the figure is mono and tabular. A disabled row has aria-disabled="true" and no link. The chevron is aria-hidden. At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard. The tone is a second sign: the row's title and meta say the same in words. The tinted text stands on its tinted ground (--*-subtle-text on --*-subtle).
purpose: A list of records one under another: transactions, documents, notifications, referrals.
usage: Use for a list read top to bottom with one main fact per row and an optional status; use a table (K24) when the reader compares columns. Do not put two links or a button inside a linked row.
notes: No tick (rule 3 of the tick: a list of rows is not a list of cards).

name: Table
accessibility: A real table: a visible caption (.ds-table__caption) names it, column headers are th scope="col", the first cell of a row is th scope="row"; numbers are end-aligned in mono. The wrapper is a role="region" with aria-labelledby the caption and tabindex="0" so a sideways scroll is reachable by keyboard. Every td carries data-label (the column name) for the phone stack; the stack turns table parts to blocks, so its markup carries explicit table roles. Header text is --text-secondary on --bg-subtle (the card ground: secondary stands there). At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Compares records across columns.
usage: Use for three or more columns the reader compares or sorts (transactions, commissions, users). Under three columns, or one fact per record, use a Row list (K23). Keep the number of columns low enough for the phone rows.

name: App shell and navigation

variants.tier_widths: bar below 880, rail from 880, wide from 1120 (media queries on a shell with no data-tier; decided by the owner, 2026-10-17); data-tier forces a tier in a specimen only, never on a product screen
parts: banner (.ds-shell__banner, above the header, the look of the warning Alert, kept at the top)
figure (.ds-header__figure, a balance or a commission as a button)
menu mark (.ds-nav__brand, from 880 with the rails, never on the tab bar)
measure (the main region is --maxw wide and centred; data-measure="wide": --maxw-wide)
toolbar (.ds-shell__toolbar: filters at the start, one primary action at the end)
action strip (.ds-shell__action: sticky above the tab bar, in the flow from 880)
frame: nav-less (.ds-shell--navless: header and main, the public storefront)

sizes: tab bar item 56 (48 minimum on a phone), rail item 48
states: sub-navigation link: rest, hover, pressed, focus, current
accessibility: Three landmarks: header, main, and one nav with an aria-label; the nav items are links and the current one has aria-current="page" (in the tab bar --primary text with the kit's --accent dot below, in the rails a --primary-subtle tint with a 2 line --primary bar at the start: not colour alone), they are not role="tab". In the icon rail the label stays in the tree as the accessible name (visually hidden). The header holds one h1; its icon buttons carry aria-label. Safe-area insets pad the bar. The nav padding keeps the focus outline inside the nav. Current item text --primary on --bg-surface in the tab bar (8.48 day, 6.72 night) and on --primary-subtle in the rails (7.61, 5.46); others --text-secondary on --bg-surface. At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard. The banner has role="status" and one line of text with its action; the header and the rail list stand below it. The back control is a link or a button with aria-label. A figure chip is a link or button whose text is its label and amount, at least --touch-min high. The menu mark is a link with aria-label. The sub-navigation is a nav with an aria-label of links, the current one aria-current="page" with the Tabs look (colour and an underline), not role=tab. The layers are the --z-* tokens.
purpose: The frame of every cabinet screen: where the user is and where else they can go.
usage: One shell per role, five nav items at most; the tier follows the viewport (bar below 880, rail from 880, wide from 1120); data-tier on .ds-shell forces one only in a specimen (a shell drawn inside a page narrower than the tier it shows); a product screen never sets it. A screen is the content of .ds-shell__main; a screen title is the header's h1. Use the Tabs (K12) to change a view in place, never for navigation between screens. A screen in main may open with the lead line, then the toolbar; its one primary action may be the sticky action strip, the last element of main. A hub under a tab uses the sub-navigation; a view changed in place is the Tabs (K12). The public storefront uses the nav-less shell.

name: Accordion

behaviour: exclusive (the same name attribute on the details)
variants.faq: ds-accordion--faq: a search above the list (input[type=search][data-faq-search] with aria-controls), a line when nothing matches (.ds-accordion__none) and a list read from the headings of a document (data-faq-source, AivisDS.faq.fromHeadings); one item at a time is the shared name attribute the component already has

accessibility: Native details and summary: the summary is the button (Enter and Space toggle it, the open state is announced by the browser), no script. The chevron is aria-hidden and turns 180 degrees when open (as the site FAQ does). The summary is at least --touch-comfortable high. Title --text-primary on --bg-surface, panel --text-secondary on --bg-surface. At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard. The search is a labelled input; the items that do not match are hidden, and the line "nothing matches" appears in the flow.
purpose: Shows many short answers or settings groups without a long page: FAQ, settings sections.
usage: Use when readers want one of several blocks; give each summary a plain question or a section name. Do not hide content a reader must see to act, and do not nest an accordion in an accordion.

name: OTP input

variants.cells: six, one digit each, in one labelled group; a left-to-right island (does not mirror)

sizes: one size: --size-3xl wide, --size-4xl high (the cabinet's cell)
accessibility: One group: role="group" named by the visible label (aria-labelledby), with the hint and the error in aria-describedby. Each cell is a text input with inputmode="numeric" and an accessible name "Digit n of 6" from the translation tables; the first cell has autocomplete="one-time-code", the others off. Typing a digit moves to the next cell; Backspace on an empty cell steps back and clears it; Left, Right, Home and End move; a paste (or an autofill that puts the whole code in one cell) fills every cell. The group is dir=ltr by CSS (direction) so digits and arrows keep their order in a right-to-left page. An invalid code sets aria-invalid="true" on every cell and shows a message with an icon and text, never colour alone. The component fires ds-otp-change and ds-otp-complete and never submits. Cells are --size-4xl high (above --touch-min). Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Entering the six digits of an e-mail or phone code.
usage: Use for a one-time code of a fixed length. The resend control and its countdown belong to the screen (a ghost button), not to the component. A longer or alphanumeric code is a text field.
notes: Cell --size-3xl by --size-4xl, --fs-h3, 700, --radius-md; the border and the focus follow the system's decided input rules (--border-input at --border-input-width, outline focus), not a 2 px border and halo; the digit is set in the mono family for figures (decided by the owner, 2026-10-17). The filled state has no look of its own: the digit is the state. No auto-submit (the code is verified by a button).

name: Date picker

variants.input: the browser's own date input, drawn as a Text field (mono figures); the period is its min and max
variants.time: input type="time", drawn the same way (the mono face, the browser's picker follows the theme)

sizes: the Text field's: sm 32, md 38 (default), lg 44
accessibility: A real input type=date with a visible label bound by for and id. The allowed period is its min and max attributes and is also written in the hint, linked by aria-describedby. An invalid value sets aria-invalid="true" and shows a message with an icon and text, linked by aria-describedby, as the Text field. The picker that opens and its keys are the browser's own; color-scheme follows the theme, so the browser's picker is dark by night. Fields are 16 px text at the 480 width. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Every Text field rule of K03 holds.
purpose: Choosing one calendar date: a document date, a filter's from and to.
usage: One input per date; a period is two inputs, the second with min set from the first by the screen. A date typed in a locale format is a text field.
notes: The cabinet uses the native date input in 4 places; the value is set in the mono family for figures. The native input is decided by the owner, 2026-10-17.

name: File input

variants.control: a secondary button (a label around the real input) and a list

sizes: button: the Button's md; item: one size, 40 thumb box --size-xl
accessibility: A real input type=file (visually hidden, still focusable) inside the label that draws the button; its name is the field's visible label (aria-labelledby) and the limits are in text under it (aria-describedby), never only in the accept attribute. The page fills data-accept, data-max-size (bytes) and the messages data-msg-type, data-msg-size, data-msg-ready, data-msg-done and data-label-remove from the translation tables. A file that fails the type or the size check is listed as an error item with its message in a role="alert" paragraph with an icon. Progress is role="progressbar" with aria-label (the file name), aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow; the status text repeats the percentage. The list is a polite live region. Each item has a remove button named "Remove <name>" (at --touch-min at the 480 width); removing returns the focus to the input. An image is previewed from a local object URL; the preview image has an empty alt because the name is beside it. The component never uploads: the app reports progress through the three calls. Focus is the system outline outside the button.
purpose: Choosing and sending documents and images (KYC, company documents, avatars, attachments).
usage: State the limits in the hint. One input per document role (front, back, selfie).
notes: The cabinet has the bare browser file input in 10 places: the item takes the Row list's and the Reorder list's look (white surface, --border-subtle, --radius-md, name display 700, meta --text-tertiary on white); the progress is the Progress component; the badge is the Badge. Decided by the owner, 2026-10-17.

name: Segmented control

variants.look: a quiet track on --bg-subtle, the chosen choice raised on --bg-surface with a --primary border

accessibility: A fieldset with a legend (visible or .ds-sr-only) holding native radios with one name: the arrow keys move and choose, the group is one tab stop, the checked radio is the selected choice. A control that switches panels is Tabs (K12). The track's outline is --border-input (3.03 day, 3.01 night on --bg-surface; 2.84 day on --bg-page) and carries no state; the selected choice is raised with a --primary border and differs in text colour, not colour alone. Selected text --primary-subtle-text on --bg-surface. At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Chooses one of two to five short options that change the view of the same content: a period, a list filter.
usage: Use for a filter or a period with short labels; for more options use a select, for panels use Tabs, for a setting that applies at once use a Toggle. Labels are single words or short phrases.

name: Auth shell
sizes: panel: --maxw-form of content plus the panel's padding
states: the screens it holds carry their own: step, error, loading
accessibility: One header landmark with the logo (one role=img named AIVIS.ONE: the mark image with empty alt and the inline wordmark aria-hidden) and the language and theme controls (ghost icon buttons with aria-label), one main landmark holding one h1 and the form, on a panel of --bg-surface (white by day, the night surface; --border-subtle border, --radius-card) over the page ground (--bg-page), centred at desktop widths and from the top on a phone. The panel is one column at every width; at the 480 width the gutter is --space-gutter-mobile, the safe-area insets pad the header, every link and control is at least --touch-min high. Text on the panel is --text-primary, --text-secondary, --primary and --danger (no amber). Reading order is logo, controls, title, text, form, links. Screens that use it (login, register, verify, reset, Telegram entry, 404) put their own form inside .ds-auth__form.
purpose: The frame of every screen before sign-in.
usage: Use for the sign-in, registration (with the demo path and the customer type), verification, password reset and onboarding screens, the Telegram first entry, and the 404 and loading pages. A screen that is not an auth screen uses the App shell (K25). The form starts from the top on a phone, on every auth screen; at desktop widths the panel is centred.
notes: A header, the title --fs-h3 700, the subtitle --fs-sm --text-secondary, the form at --maxw-form, over the page ground; the phone rules (gutter, safe areas, touch targets) follow the system's phone rules. The header puts the logo at the start and the controls at the end on every auth screen. The logo is the colour mark brand/aivis-mark.svg (an image, --size-sm, unchanged) and the wordmark of brand/aivis-wordmark.svg inline in currentColor (--text-primary), half the mark's height, --space-3 apart; the lockup image is not used here because its lettering has no fill and goes dark at night. The form sits on a --bg-surface panel and starts from the top on a phone: decided by the owner, 2026-10-17.

name: Nav tile

variants.layout: a wide row tile: icon at the start, title and a line of text, chevron at the end; one column on a phone

sizes: one size, at least touch-min high
accessibility: The whole tile is one anchor (never a div with a click handler); its name is the title and description. A tile that cannot be opened carries aria-disabled="true" and no href. The icon box is decorative (aria-hidden icon); the badge is text. The tile is at least --touch-min high. Title --text-primary and description --text-secondary on --bg-surface. At the 480 width and below every interactive part is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: A door from a hub (More, a dashboard) to one screen.
usage: Use for a grid of destinations with an icon and a title; use a Row list (K23) when each destination carries a value or a status. One tile, one link, one icon from the set; no more than a dozen tiles on a screen.

name: Structured payout form

variants.layout: fieldsets with legends, a field grid of one column on a phone and two from --center-lg per column up

sizes: fields at the Text field's sizes
accessibility: A form named by its heading (aria-labelledby). Each group is a fieldset with a legend; every field is a labelled Text field with its hint and message in aria-describedby; an invalid field has aria-invalid="true" and a message with an icon and text, and an Alert (role=alert) names how many fields need a look. A locked form (a withdrawal is open) disables the fieldsets and says why in an Alert (role=status). Saving sets aria-busy on the form and on the Button (loading, label kept). The component carries no limit, fee, price or payment term as content: the limits are shown by the screen from the platform settings. At the 480 width the action buttons are full width and every field is at least --touch-min high.
purpose: Entering payout details and a withdrawal amount as fields instead of a raw JSON text box.
usage: Which fields a payout needs, and in which order, is the app's (the backender's payout schema); this component is the form around them. Amounts take the Text field's --num (mono figures).
notes: A form of existing parts (Text field K03, Button K01, Alert K09, Card K07); the only new rules are the fieldset and the grid. The fields in the specimen are an example, not a decision of the payout schema.

name: Combobox / user picker

variants.filter: data-filter="local" filters the options in the page; absent, the app replaces the options on ds-combobox-query
variants.chosen: a chip with Clear, as the cabinet's picker

sizes: the Text field's md; options --size-3xl high, --touch-min at the 480 width
accessibility: The ARIA 1.2 combobox: an input with role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls (the listbox id), aria-autocomplete="list" and aria-activedescendant naming the option the keyboard is on; a ul role="listbox" named by the label of the field, each option role="option" with an id and aria-selected; aria-disabled for an option that cannot be chosen. Focus stays in the input. Down opens and moves, Up moves back, Home and End go to the first and the last option while the list is open, Enter chooses, Escape closes (and then empties the text). A polite status (role=status, text from data-msg-count and data-msg-none) says how many results there are; the empty message is text. The active option is a tint and a bar at the start, never colour alone. Choosing shows a chip with the option's avatar, name and detail and a Clear button (aria-label from the translation tables) that returns the focus to the input. data-min-chars holds the shortest search the app wants. The component fires ds-combobox-query and ds-combobox-select; debounce and the request are the app's. Focus is the system outline on the input.
purpose: Finding one record by typing: a user by name or e-mail, a company.
usage: Use when the list is too long for a select (more than about ten). The result detail line holds what tells two people apart (e-mail, role).
notes: A bordered result list --radius-md, a 32 px avatar, name --fs-sm 600, detail --fs-xs --text-secondary, a chip on --bg-subtle; the roles and the keys are those of the combobox; the result list stands on --bg-surface; the avatar is an initials disc (--primary, --on-primary, 700).

name: Reorder list

variants.order: an ordered list (ol) with a position figure

sizes: rows --size-lg or taller; move buttons --size-sm by --size-xs (the cabinet's), --touch-min at the 480 width
states: first and last (the button that cannot move is disabled)
accessibility: An ol named by a visible heading (aria-labelledby); each row has a Move up and a Move down button whose accessible name includes the row's title ("Move Prototype review up", from data-label-up and data-label-down); the button that cannot move is disabled. After a move the focus stays on the same button (or the other one when this one is now at an end), the row carries data-moved until the focus leaves it, and a polite status (data-live names its element, text from data-msg-moved with {name}, {n} and {total}) says where the row went. The position figure is aria-hidden: the ol already gives the order. Keyboard operation is the buttons' own (Tab, Enter, Space). The component fires ds-reorder-change with the new order of the rows' data-id and never saves it. Buttons are at least --touch-min square at the 480 width. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Putting a short list in order: roadmap steps, attachments, documents.
usage: Use for lists of up to a few dozen rows. A pointer drag is not built (the cabinet has none): buttons only. A list that sorts itself is not this component.
notes: A pair of small up and down buttons at the start of the row, 1 px border, --radius-sm, a --text-secondary glyph, primary on hover; the rest of the row takes the Row list's surface. The move button border is --border-input, the system's outlined-button border (3.03 and 3.01 against white), not --border-default.

name: Language and theme controls (CAppControls)
accessibility: No component is built here: the cabinet code is not changed by this batch. The contract is in components.md, section "K40 contract".
purpose: Switch language and theme.
usage: See components.md.
notes: Labels come from i18n keys, never from English literals in the template.

name: Action menu

variants.align: data-align="end" opens toward the end edge
variants.listbox: single choice: button[aria-haspopup="listbox"], ul[role=listbox] of button[role=option][aria-selected]; the chosen option carries the check, a flag slot may stand first

sizes: the trigger is a Button (sm 32, md 38, lg 44); items --size-xl high, --touch-min at the 480 width
states: item focus (the outline outside the item, in the list's padding)
accessibility: The menu button pattern. The trigger is a button with aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls (the list id); the list is ul role="menu" named by the button (aria-labelledby), each action a button role="menuitem" inside li role="none", a rule is li role="separator". Enter, Space and Down open and focus the first item, Up opens on the last; in the list Up and Down move and wrap, Home and End go to the ends, a typed letter moves to the next item that starts with it, Escape closes and returns the focus to the button, Tab closes, a click outside closes; an item with aria-disabled stays in the list and is skipped. The menu never acts itself: ds-menu-select carries the item value and the app acts. At the 480 width every item is at least --touch-min high. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard. The listbox follows the menu's keys and opens on the chosen option; the chosen option is marked by the check icon and the tint, not by colour alone. The languages come from the shared setting, never from a list written in a screen.
purpose: Offer a short list of actions for one object: the share actions of a hub link (A-2) and the row actions of a staff list (S-2).
usage: Use for three to seven actions that do not fit on the row. A destructive action takes the danger item and the app asks for confirmation. A choice of a value is a select or a combobox, not this menu. The trigger is a Button with the share icon before its word and the chevron after it. A language list is this listbox variant.
notes: No AIVIS source holds an action menu (map K26: MISSING; the cabinet language picker is a listbox), so the look is built from the system: the surface, border, radius and shadow of the combobox list, the row hover tint of the Row list. The open trigger takes --bg-subtle and the chevron turns, as the accordion chevron does.

name: Stepper and schedule list

variants.orientation: vertical (default); data-orientation="horizontal" in a row from 640 up, stacked below
variants.schedule row: default, aria-current="step" (the current item), data-status="problem" (a tinted item that needs attention)
variants.dots: ds-dots: n dots, the current one wider (aria-current="step"), with the position said in words

sizes: marker --size-xl; schedule stats in columns of at least --center-sm
accessibility: An ordered list (ol) named by aria-label or aria-labelledby; the step in progress carries aria-current="step". A state is never colour alone: done holds a check icon, problem a triangle, current and upcoming their number, and the meta line says the state in words; the markers are aria-hidden. The schedule is an ol of rows; each row has a title and a Badge with the state in words; the current row carries aria-current="step"; a dl of stats and a foot line are optional and the screen fills them. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard. Step dots: the list has an aria-label with the position ("Step 2 of 4"); the current dot differs in width, not only in colour; the dots reach 3:1 against the surface (--border-input).
purpose: Show progress through a flow (purchase, onboarding, KYC) and the review steps of a document.
usage: Use the stepper for three to six steps in a fixed order; the schedule list for a list of items that each have a state. The connector line is decoration; the state is read from the marker and the words.
notes: The schedule rows are bordered rows on the page ground, the problem row on --danger-subtle with a --danger border, a three column stats grid, with status badges; the labels use --text-secondary because tertiary does not stand on the page ground by day. The stepper's look is built from the Badge and Progress vocabulary: success for done, primary for current, danger for problem.

name: Document sheet and viewer

variants.placement: data-variant="sheet" (a bottom sheet, the cabinet AgreementSheet) or "modal" (centred, the cabinet LegalDocModal)
variants.inline: --inline draws the dialog in the flow of a page
variants.content: in-page HTML, or a sandboxed iframe (ds-docviewer__frame)

sizes: sheet up to --maxw-prose; modal up to --maxw-form-wide; at most 90dvh high
accessibility: A dialog: role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby naming its heading, tabindex="-1" so the focus can enter it. The focus moves to the dialog on open, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, Escape, the close button and a click on the veil close it, and the focus returns to the button that opened it (components.js). The body is a scrollable region with tabindex="0" and a name so the keyboard can scroll it. A download is a real link (a with the app href and download). An iframe keeps sandbox="" and a title. Loading sets aria-busy and a status text; an error is an Alert with role="alert". At the 480 width the actions take the full width and the sheet starts from the safe-area inset. The page behind is not made inert and its scroll is not locked by this component. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Read a document (a purchase agreement, an ownership certificate, a legal text of the sign-up) and take a copy of it.
usage: Use the sheet for a document opened from a row of a position and the modal for the legal texts of the sign-up, as the cabinet does. The component carries no price and no payment term; the text is the app document. The veil behind the dialog is the token --scrim; in-page text follows the theme; the frame of a sandboxed document is --paper, white in both themes.
notes: The sheet: a 60 percent high framed document on a white canvas, Close and Save in a row, the loading and error states, on a page-ground sheet with a deep shadow and a 520 wide cap; the modal: a framed scrolling body with prose styles. The veil is --scrim, --neutral-950 at 50 percent in both themes. The document paints no ground, so the frame is --paper, white in both themes. An Email button is the screen's, not part of the component.

name: Document row with download
sizes: the Row list row; --touch-min high at the 480 width
states: unavailable (aria-disabled, no link, full opacity: its text carries the state)
accessibility: A Row list row whose title and meta sit inside ONE real link (a with href and download), so the link name carries the file type and size in text ("Signed agreement PDF, 218 KB, English"). The trailing icon is decorative. The state is also said in words in a status element (role="status") filled from data-msg-downloading, data-msg-downloaded and data-msg-failed on the row. An unavailable row has no link and says in text that the file is not there yet (aria-disabled="true"). Focus is the Row list outline around the row. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Download a file listed in a screen: attachments of a company, documents of a staff or an investor, the signed agreement of a booking.
usage: Use it for any file a screen lists. The file type and size come from the file, formatted in the page language. A file that is not uploaded yet is the unavailable row, never a dead link. In the cabinet the href is the file's route and the app handles the click (an API call for a short-lived presigned link, then a navigation: frontend/src/api/attachments.ts), then calls AivisDS.docrow.done or .fail; nothing calls done for a plain download link, so the app does.
notes: An icon box, a title, the description, the file name and size, a download icon; the download is a real link, not a button; on the Row list (K23).

name: Booking card

variants.kind: a Badge says the basis in words: purchase, gift
variants.pdf: the signed agreement row is a K44 link, or the unavailable row

sizes: a Card (md); the facts wrap in columns of at least --center-sm
states: the agreement button: rest, hover, pressed, focus
accessibility: An article named by its heading (aria-labelledby). The facts are a dl (booked date, units). The basis is a sentence. The agreement as HTML opens K36 from a button; the signed agreement is a K44 row. The icon box is aria-hidden; the kind is in the badge text. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Show one purchase of an investor's position with its basis and its two documents.
usage: One card per purchase. The card carries the amount paid for the purchase, as the app gives it, and never the price of a part or a payment term (decided by the owner, 2026-10-23, correcting the rule of 2026-10-14). KN1 is a placeholder id.
notes: An icon by basis, the kind, the date, the units, the amount paid, a view button, on the Card (K07), with the K44 row for the PDF and the K36 button.

name: Invoice and QR block
sizes: the QR pad up to --center-md plus --size-4xl wide; the copy button full width at the 480 width
states: copied (data-state="copied", a check and a word)
accessibility: A section named by a heading. The fields are a dl. The QR is an img with alt text that says what it is; the same address is text in a selectable element (dir="ltr"), so the data is never only in the picture. The Copy button names its action; on success components.js switches its label and icon (data-label-copied) and writes the confirmation into a role="status" element (polite), and puts the button back after three seconds; a failure writes data-msg-failed. When the invoice is expired or the QR cannot be drawn the image is hidden and a sentence says why. The QR and the address are left-to-right islands (direction: ltr). Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Pay a deposit: the invoice fields, the QR and the address to copy.
usage: The app fills the network, the amount and the deadline; the component writes no amount, fee or term. The QR pad is white in both themes because a camera scanner needs dark on white; the QR image is the app's. No value of a wallet is stored by the component. The copy script is shared with the Copyable value (K53), which is the same job outside an invoice.
notes: The three fields, the QR and the address; the QR is drawn in a forced light palette. The pad is --paper, white in both themes, because a camera scanner needs dark on white. A warning card is an Alert of the system.

name: Bar chart with a text alternative

variants.axis: follows the reading direction (the labels by their grid, the svg turned end for end by scale: -1 1 under :dir(rtl), so the first bar stands under the first label)
variants.peak: data-peak on the highest bar (a darker fill and an outline, a shade apart from a plain bar; the range line names the peak in words)

sizes: plot --center-lg high; one column per month
accessibility: The bars are an svg with role="img" and aria-labelledby naming the title and a line that gives the range and the peak. The same numbers are a real table (th scope, a caption or region name) in a details element that is open by default: the text alternative. The svg holds no text; the month labels are an HTML list hidden from the accessibility tree because the table names them. A bar is never the only carrier: the range line names the peak in words, every value is in the table, and the bars are one series in --primary on --bg-surface. No hover tooltip is required. Empty data shows a sentence in place of the svg. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Show a series by month on the analytics screen of a company (C-4).
usage: One series, oldest first; the height is value / max with a value above zero at least one row. A second series needs a design of its own (patterns, labels) and is not built. The chart is stretched to the width by preserveAspectRatio="none", so the bars have square corners (the cabinet's flex bars have a rounded top).
notes: A --bg-surface plot with a border, --primary bars, a 3xs uppercase month label; the plot is --center-lg, 320 high; the values are carried by the table, not by title-attribute tooltips. The month labels use --text-secondary: they stand on the plot's --bg-surface, where tertiary would be allowed by day; secondary is darker for the 3xs uppercase size. The row of month labels follows the reading direction, and so does this chart.

name: Checkbox

use: agreement or consent (a tick, never a switch)
a group of permissions in a fieldset

sizes: a row of at least 40, at least --touch-min high at the 480 width; the box is --size-2xs
accessibility: A native input[type=checkbox] inside a label, so the whole row is the target and the name is the text; the box is decorative. Links inside the text open their pages and do not toggle the box. An invalid box takes aria-invalid="true" and a .ds-field__error message under it. A group is a fieldset with a legend. The checked box is --primary with --on-primary (8.48 day, 5.85 night) and its border reaches 3:1 against the surface (--border-input 3.03 day, 3.01 night). Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: A tick the person sets to agree or to choose.
usage: An agreement stays a tick ("it is like a signature"), never a Toggle; a setting that applies at once is a Toggle (K06). The label may hold links to the documents agreed to. Use one markup everywhere: the cabinet had three.

name: Stat tile

layout: .ds-stats: two across on a phone, as many as fit above

sizes: one size; the tiles fill the columns of .ds-stats (--tile-min)
accessibility: A label above a figure, read in that order. The change is said in text with its sign and repeated by an arrow icon, so it is never colour alone; --success and --danger stand on the white surface (6.30 and 7.86 day). An interactive tile holds one link in its label that stretches over the tile; no click handler on the container. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: A figure with its label, and often how it moved.
usage: Use it for a KPI or a balance line; a summary on the primary colour is the brand Card (K07). The app writes the figure, the unit and the sign.

name: Hero
accessibility: A section named by its title (aria-labelledby). The picture is decorative (alt=""): the title says what it is. Every text on it is --text-on-scrim over --scrim-strong, so it reaches 7.63 on a white photo, 13.81 on a mid-grey one and 20.17 on a black one (tokens/contrast.json), in both themes, because a photo does not change with the theme. The veil under the text is at full strength and fades only over the padding above the first line.
purpose: A cover with the title laid over the photo.
usage: The text over a photo is --text-on-scrim and the veil is --scrim-strong; the flat --scrim does not reach 4.5 over a bright photo. A product, a purchase, an instalment, a public product or a company overview opens with it.

name: Empty state
accessibility: An icon (decorative), a heading, a description capped at --maxw-prose and an actions slot. A failed load takes role="alert"; the title and the text say it in words and the danger tint is only a second sign. Buttons keep their own focus.
purpose: Nothing here yet, or the load failed, with the way forward.
usage: Use it where a list, a page or a section has no content; it is not a message in context (Alert, K09) and not a loading state (Skeleton, K19). Give it a Retry button when the cause is a failed load, a Create or Open button when it is just empty.

name: Key-value list
accessibility: A dl with a div around each dt and dd, which the accessibility tree reads as pairs. The values are text in the mono face with tabular figures.
purpose: One pair per row: a term at the start and its value at the end.
usage: Use it for a price breakdown, a balance line, the fields of an invoice or the details of a transaction inside a Card or a Dialog. The Booking card (KN1) and the Invoice block (K43) keep their own facts lists.

name: Avatar
accessibility: A photo is an img with alt text naming the person or the company; initials are a span with role="img" and aria-label, or aria-hidden when the name stands beside the disc. The initials are --on-primary on --primary (8.48 day, 5.85 night).
purpose: Who a person or a company is, in one disc.
usage: A company logo disc is an Avatar. The combobox (K38) keeps its own 32 px disc as its slot.

name: Chat thread and composer
sizes: a bubble is at most 520 wide
accessibility: The feed is a ul with role="log", aria-live="polite" and tabindex="0" so a keyboard user can scroll it. Own and other messages are told apart by the side and the ground and, in staff views, by the author line, not by colour alone. Text is --text-primary on --primary-subtle or --bg-subtle (16.0 or better day). The composer is a labelled textarea and a Button. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: A conversation: messages in a feed and a field to write the next one.
usage: The screen gives the thread its height; the feed scrolls and the composer stays under it.

name: Dialog

placement: sheet (default: from the bottom, a cap of --maxw-prose)

sizes: sheet or modal; at most 90dvh high, the body scrolls
accessibility: role="dialog" or "alertdialog" with aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby the title and, for a confirm, aria-describedby the text. components.js moves the focus to the panel on open, keeps Tab inside, closes on Escape and on a click on the scrim (data-lock="true" keeps the scrim from closing it) and returns the focus to what opened it. The close button is a ghost icon button with aria-label. A destructive confirm is a danger Button and the cancel stays first in the order of reading. Events ds-dialog-open and ds-dialog-close are the app's hooks.
purpose: A confirm, an edit form or the details of an item, over the page.
usage: Use it for anything that is not a document; the document sheet and viewer (K36) keeps the framed body, Close and Save of a document. A confirm says what will happen in the text and puts the action in the button.

name: Copyable value
sizes: one size; the button is a small ghost icon button
accessibility: The value is selectable text (user-select: all) and a left-to-right island. The button has an aria-label that names the value; components.js writes the result into the polite status line (data-msg-copied, data-msg-failed) and switches the icon to a check, with the clipboard and a selection copy as the fallback. The copied tint is --success on --bg-subtle (5.55 day). Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: A value to copy: a code, a link, a hash, a secret.
usage: Use it for a referral code or link, a transaction hash, a two-factor secret. The Invoice block (K43) keeps its own copy button and shares the script.

name: Timeline
accessibility: An ordered list with an aria-label. The marker is decorative; the state is said by the Badge or the title, not by the marker alone. An opening entry is native details and summary (Enter and Space toggle it) with a chevron that turns. Dates are time elements. Focus is a --focus-width solid outline in --focus-ring at --focus-offset, outside the part. Motion is under the reduced-motion guard.
purpose: Dated milestones of a project, in order.
usage: Use it where the dates matter and an entry has a body; progress through a flow is the Stepper (K32).
